goal: Links should not live forever by default: give new links a sensible, human-approved default lifetime without breaking existing links or clients
functional: Links created without an explicit expiry receive a default expiry (length decided by a human)
Clients may still request an explicit expiry, up to a maximum (decided by a human)
Whether links with a custom alias also receive the default expiry is decided by a human
Expired links keep returning HTTP 410 and their statistics stay readable
constraints: Existing links, including permanent ones, are never modified or migrated
No change to routes, payloads or public Python signatures: new parameters must be optional

ambiguities.question: How long should a new link live when the client gives no expiry?
ambiguities.why: Changes the lifetime of every future link; a wrong answer silently breaks links people have already shared

ambiguities.question: What is the longest expiry a client may request?
ambiguities.why: Keeping today's ceiling avoids rejecting requests that work now

ambiguities.question: Should links with a custom alias also get the default expiry?
ambiguities.why: Aliases are usually deliberate campaign links; expiring them unasked would surprise their owners

acceptance: A link created without a ttl expires after the decided default and then returns 410
An explicit ttl overrides the default, and a ttl above the decided maximum is rejected
Alias links follow the decision on whether the default applies to them
Existing permanent links, idempotent re-shortening and the public API are unchanged
Every decision is visible in the code, covered by a test, and recorded in the changelog
